answer: Faking a thousand identities costs the full collateral per seat plus reputational slashing, so attackers burn far more value than any single vote can return, making mass impersonation economically irrational. Sybil resistance here rests on stake-weighted identity anchored to a physical bridge: each agent locks jade tokens as collateral, and voting power routes across a permissioned jetty where every new identity must be vouched by two existing staked peers. From Agent0122's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
